decision_points.question: which regression model and standard-error scheme is used to estimate the skin-tone effect?
decision_points.why_rival: each is a complete, mutually-exclusive primary-model specification (logistic vs linear-probability/OLS, with clustered / HC3 / no-cluster SEs); an analyst fits exactly one estimator

decision_points.question: which covariates make up the model's adjustment set?
decision_points.why_rival: each names, adds to, or removes from the set of controls; the analyst settles on one covariate configuration for the model

decision_points.question: how is games-played entered into the model (functional form / transformation)?
decision_points.why_rival: log with +1 offset, log with 0.5 offset, floor-then-log, quadratic term, natural spline, and spline-swapped-for-log are rival ways to encode the same games variable; only one form is used

decision_points.question: what minimum number of shared games per dyad is required for inclusion?
decision_points.why_rival: each sets the exposure threshold to a different cutoff (or drops it entirely); the dyad inclusion rule is a single choice

decision_points.question: are players with too few total games excluded as a data-quality filter?
decision_points.why_rival: a player-level low-activity QC exclusion, distinct in purpose and unit from the per-dyad exposure threshold

decision_points.question: how is the skin-tone predictor operationalized — kept as a full continuous range or dichotomized at a threshold?
decision_points.why_rival: keeping the full continuous skin-tone range and dichotomizing at a cutoff (and sweeping which cutoff) are rival treatments of the exposure; choosing one precludes the other

decision_points.question: how is the red-card outcome operationalized?
decision_points.why_rival: constructing a smoothed per-game red-card rate is one way to define the outcome variable

decision_points.question: is the skin-tone effect compared between a minimally-adjusted (games-only) and a fully-adjusted model?
decision_points.why_rival: a diagnostic contrasting adjustment sets to gauge confounding impact

decision_points.question: how is the fitted model's calibration assessed?
decision_points.why_rival: comparing in-sample predicted probabilities against observed rates is one calibration-check approach

decision_points.question: how is systematic missingness in skin-tone ratings assessed?
decision_points.why_rival: comparing distributions between dyads with vs without skin-tone data is one way to probe non-random missingness

decision_points.question: how is covariate balance across skin-tone groups checked?
decision_points.why_rival: crosstabbing position against skin-tone group is one balance-diagnostic approach

decision_points.question: are game-frequency weights applied when fitting the model?
decision_points.why_rival: weighting vs not weighting observations by games played is a single weighting choice

decision_points.question: what baseline N is used to account for sample exclusions?
decision_points.why_rival: using a hardcoded original N of 146028 is one convention for exclusion reporting
